newsitem.title: DUBAI: SABIC to produce 28mln tonnes by year 200.
newsitem.headline: SABIC to produce 28mln tonnes by year 200.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's petrochemical industrial heavyweight Saudi Basic Industries Corp said on Sunday it planned to reach annual total production capacity of 28 million tonnes by the year 2000 from 23 million tonnes now.
SABIC Vice-Chairman Ibrahim bin Abdullah bin Salameh said increased output would come from building new projects and expanding existing ones.

"This is part of SABIC's constant efforts to boost its position on the world's industrial and marketing map," he said in the statement issued by the company's headquarters in Riyadh and faxed to Reuters. He gave no further details.
SABIC, which produces about five percent of the world's petrochemicals, is 70 percent owned by the Saudi government.
It has predicted lower net profits for full-year 1996 despite an increase in production and sales because of depressed prices worldwide.
It posted a record 6.28 billion riyals ($1.67 billion) profit in 1995, up from 4.20 billion riyals in 1994. ($1 = 3.75 riyals)
